beats.narration_text: Namaste. This is Liam, in for Bear. A long-running agent will tell you it's done. The real question is how you make it prove it.

props.text:

beats.motion_claim: The writer types the naive question (how to get an agent to say it's done) and corrects it to the real one (how to make it prove it).

beats.narration_text: Three terms. The builder: the agent session that writes the feature. The evaluator: a separate agent that checks the work. And default-FAIL: every check starts as failing, until evidence proves it passes.

beats.narration_text: Here's a long-running agent as a workshop. At the bench, a builder makes one feature at a time. Left alone, it grades itself: after one unit test, it marks the part passing, even when the screen is visibly broken.

shot.visual_intent: A kraft workbench with the dark builder station slides in; the station's light comes on; a kraft part crate rises out of the bench; a crack draws across its face; the builder slaps its own PASS tag on it anyway.
shot.motion_claim: A kraft workbench with the dark builder station slides in; the station's light comes on; a kraft part crate rises out of the bench; a crack draws across its face; the builder slaps its own PASS tag on it anyway.

beats.narration_text: Asking nicely doesn't reliably stop that. So the harness flips the default. Every feature is a row in test-results dot json, and every row starts false.

shot.visual_intent: A prompt note slides to the station and the PASS tag stays put; on 'flips the default' the PASS tag flies off and a FAIL tag drops on; the results board slides in and three rows each draw an ink cross.

beats.narration_text: A hook guards that file. The builder can't write to it until it has opened evidence: a screenshot, a console log. Each read unlocks one write. The next change needs fresh proof.

beats.narration_text: Then a second agent inspects the work, from its own booth, with a fresh context. It never saw the build. It gets the spec, the diff and the screenshots, and it has no Write or Edit tools.

shot.visual_intent: A wall rises beside the bench, leaving the builder's reasoning pages behind it; a closed kraft booth slides in on the far side; a spec page, a diff card and the screenshot slide through a hatch into the booth; a pencil beside the booth is crossed out.

beats.narration_text: Its instructions say plausibility is not correctness, and missing evidence means needs work. So it answers PASS or needs work, and its findings become the next build session's first prompt.

shot.visual_intent: Inside the booth's window the screenshot's crack is circled; the booth's lamp comes on; a NEEDS_WORK slip slides out; a findings note rides back over the wall to the builder station; the part's tag flips back to FAIL.

beats.narration_text: Each session starts cold. So the builder keeps its own handoff note, PROGRESS dot md, and reads it first on every restart. It commits as it goes, and a hook commits what's left when the session stops.

shot.visual_intent: The builder station's light goes out and a fresh station slides in; a clipboard on the bench fills with lines; it lifts toward the station on 'reads it first'; grey commit slabs drop onto a git-log stack; the light goes out and one last slab drops.

beats.narration_text: Put it together and it's a loop: build, inspect, rebuild, until no row says false, a cycle changes nothing, or the budget runs out. Want true to mean the inspector agreed? Let only its PASS write the row.

shot.visual_intent: A conveyor loop joins the bench and the booth; parts ride out to the booth and back; the board above flips its rows from cross to check one at a time; a dashed line runs from the booth to the board.

beats.narration_text: And you stay in charge. Create a file called agent stop, and every tool call halts. Write a note in STEER dot md, and the agent sees it once, mid-run, with no restart.

shot.visual_intent: The loop is running; an AGENT_STOP file card drops beside it and every light goes grey, the part frozen on the belt; the file lifts away and the lights come back; a STEER note slides to the builder station and vanishes once read.

beats.narration_text: Claude Code also has a built-in checker. Slash goal takes a condition, and after every turn a separate fast model checks it until it's met. Write your own evaluator dot md when you want your own inspector and the evidence gate.

shot.visual_intent: A small dark /goal booth with a one-line condition card; parts pass it turn by turn and its lamp blinks each time until a check lands; then the kraft evaluator.md booth with the hook gate in front slides in beside it.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude Code: Help me write a default-FAIL evaluator for one long task: name your task. Save it as dot claude, slash agents, slash evaluator dot md, with no Write or Edit tools. List the exact conditions it must see to pass, and the evidence that proves each one: a screenshot, a console log, or a test result. It reviews only the spec, the diff and that evidence, never the builder's reasoning. Its first line is PASS or needs work; missing evidence is needs work. Don't build the task. Then check two things yourself. Hand it a commit with no screenshot. Does it say needs work? And open evaluator dot md. Does its tools line leave out Write and Edit?

It reviews only the spec, the diff and that evidence, never the builder's reasoning. Its first line is PASS or NEEDS_WORK; missing evidence is NEEDS_WORK. Don't build the task.
